headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: nullclaw’s filesystem/workspace access plus LightAgent’s broad egress and MCP create a dangerous default pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent can use MCP and parse external content, while nullclaw exposes multiple inbound channels and browser/web surfaces. The pair has a plausible instruction-hijack path if nullclaw forwards web or webhook content into LightAgent without provenance checks. This is not proven by direct pair evidence, so uncertainty is kept at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF nullclaw forwards webhook, web, or browser content into LightAgent prompts without sanitization
IF LightAgent consumes MCP payloads as trusted instructions
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all cross-agent messages
Strip instructions from fetched web content before forwarding
Disable MCP forwarding for untrusted sources
requires-engineering: enforce allowlisted message schemas between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch sensitive conversational and secret-bearing data, and nullclaw has workspace files plus broad read/write surfaces while LightAgent has broad network egress and handles API keys/TOT keys. In the default pair, data can move from shared workspace or conversation state into LightAgent’s outbound APIs, creating realistic exfiltration risk. The blast radius includes secrets and audit data.
conditions: IF either agent stores secrets or conversation history in the shared workspace
IF LightAgent sends retrieved workspace contents to external APIs
mitigations: Move secrets out of shared workspace
Restrict LightAgent egress to approved domains
Separate per-agent workspaces
Rotate any exposed API keys
requires-engineering: add content-classification gates before outbound requests

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightAgent can spawn subprocesses and use MCP, while nullclaw can execute shell, modify git state, read/write the filesystem, and also supports multiple instances with shared durable memory. That overlap creates a direct write/write conflict on shared mutable resources, especially git and workspace state, with no locking mechanism documented here. Uncertainty about orchestration should be treated as dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or git repository
IF either agent runs concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate repositories per agent
Disable concurrent writes
Add a file-locking wrapper around git operations
Pause one agent during the other’s write phase
requires-engineering: implement optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: nullclaw’s multi-channel agent stack can treat upstream outputs as workflow inputs, and LightAgent can generate tool results, browser output, and MCP payloads that may be forwarded. If nullclaw acts on LightAgent outputs without verification, errors can cascade into emails, CRM actions, or other downstream side effects. The pair’s default automation posture makes this a high-risk chain.
conditions: IF nullclaw uses LightAgent output as authoritative input
IF downstream actions are triggered without human review
mitigations: Require human approval for downstream actions
Add a verification step before acting on LightAgent output
Log source provenance on every forwarded field
Limit LightAgent to draft-only mode
requires-engineering: add structured validation of all inter-agent outputs

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent explicitly handles API keys, TOT keys, and user conversations, while nullclaw handles private keys, bearer tokens, service-account JSON, audit logs, and workspace files. Even without a documented residency mismatch, the pair clearly mixes regulated and secret-bearing data classes across two open-source agents with broad egress and storage surfaces. The compliance gap is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated or secret-bearing data is routed through both agents
IF retention or residency policies differ between their storage locations
mitigations: Classify data before routing it between agents
Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Align retention settings across both systems
Review outbound destinations for residency constraints
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing
